title: Real standard cells (SkyWater sky130)
what: The hello lock after it was turned into real SkyWater sky130 logic cells, the way a chip factory receives it. No Verilog source is needed: only the cell netlist and the cell library.
why: The chip that is made is the cell netlist, not the source code. Protections must survive into it.
teaches: GlitchSAT reads what each cell does from the library file, checks every cell by its truth table, and asks the same question on the real cells.

runs.label: 2. Run the protected lock (sky130)
runs.expect: no attack with up to 2 glitches

lesson_after: Same answers as for the Verilog version, now on factory cells: the protected lock's three checks survived into this sky130 netlist because it was mapped one module at a time. A flow that flattens before optimising (LibreLane's default, like the hello lock's `synth` build) can merge the three copies, so always check the netlist that is really made. These netlists also use the isolation cell lpflow_inputiso1p as a plain OR gate; real flows list lpflow cells as don't-use. Needs the sky130 library on this computer (scripts/fetch_libs.sh).
